title: gnaphalium microcephalum subsp. thermale
intro: Gnaphalium microcephalum subsp. thermale, commonly known as a type of daisy, is a plant species that belongs to the family Asteraceae. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties and is valued for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities. The bioactive constituents of Gnaphalium microcephalum subsp. thermale include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, such as pain relief, wound healing, and antiseptic properties. Further research is needed to fully understand the plant's efficacy and potential uses in traditional medicine.
